related.excerpt: One of CIA’s oldest and most recognizable intelligence publications, The World Factbook, has sunset. The World Factbook served the Intelligence Community and the general public as a longstanding, one-stop basic reference about countries and communities around the globe. Let’s take a quick look into the history of The World Factbook. Over many decades, The World Factbook evolved from a classified to unclassified, hardcopy to electronic product that added new categories, and even new global entities. The original classified publication, titled The National Basic Intelligence Factbook, launched in 1962. The first unclassified companion version was issued in 1971. A decade later it was renamed The World Factbook. In 1997, The World Factbook went digital and debuted to a worldwide audience on CIA.gov, where it garnered millions of views each year. The World Factbook appealed to researchers, news organizations, teachers, students, and international travelers. related.title: Afghanistan: WFP Aghanistan Country Brief, July 2026 (pdf)
related.summary: SITUATION OVERVIEW • Regional conflicts are exacerbating the humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan, with staple food prices at elevated levels and transport costs tripling due to prolonged border closure with Pakistan, re-routed supply chains due to the conflict in the Middle East, and increased fuel prices. • In addition, funding constraints have compelled WFP to suspend cash assistance for returnees from Iran and Pakistan at all border crossings, leaving vulnerable families without critical support upon arrival.
bullets: SITUATION OVERVIEW • Regional conflicts are exacerbating the humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan, with staple food prices at elevated levels and transport costs tripling due to prolonged border closure with Pakistan, re-routed supply chains due to the conflict in the Middle East, and increased fuel prices.

• In addition, funding constraints have compelled WFP to suspend cash assistance for returnees from Iran and Pakistan at all border crossings, leaving vulnerable families without critical support upon arrival.
• Funding constraints have also forced WFP to suspend cash assistance at all border crossings, leaving vulnerable returning families without critical support.
These supply chain pressures are particularly acute for imported specialized nutritious foods (SNFs), with most WFP-supported health clinics currently facing a stock out of these commodities.

Support focused on strengthening food security, climate resilience, and livelihoods through community asset creation, skills development, agricultural and livestock assistance, and cash-based support.
related.excerpt: Reporting Period: June 2026 Photo Caption & Credit: Children at Maiwand Primary School in Paktika province receive fortiﬁed biscuits. WFP/Isheeta Sumra AFGHANISTAN COUNTRY BRIEF JULY 2026 IN NUMBERS 1.9 million people assisted in June 2026 (49% female) 2,700 mt food distributed in June 2026 USD 6.9 M cash transferred in June 2026 USD 492 M (July – Dec 2026) net funding requirements KEY HIGHLIGHTS • After a prolonged pipeline break, more than 1,600 mt of the approximately 6,000 mt of nutrition commodities expected in the country have arrived, enabling WFP to reach 80,000 children and 25,000 mothers. • Since early July, funding shortfalls have forced WFP to suspend famine-prevention programmes in hotspot areas, putting 1.5 million people at risk of life-threatening hunger. • Funding constraints have also forced WFP to suspend cash assistance at all border crossings, leaving vulnerable returning families without critical support.
